nodes.label: Derive the expected column shape from the desktop app's own schema source, not a hardcoded list
nodes.norm_label: derive expectation from app source not a hardcoded list
nodes.summary: The new integration test init_column_shapes_match_what_the_desktop_app_declares computes every expectation at run time by parsing the app's own CREATE TABLE blocks in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/database/schema.rs and the ALTER TABLE column definitions in schema_migrations.rs, resolved from env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"). It then runs the real snipset binary through the existing run helper and compares against pragma_table_info. No expected column list, type, or default is written into the test.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L37] A test that restates the list shares the blind spot it is supposed to catch, so the expectation has to come from the source that actually decides the live shape; this mirrors the philosophy already stated in fingerprint_test.rs.

nodes.label: column_definition catch-all arm
nodes.summary: Reused id. Same claim, counted independently in this session. The listed arms of column_definition in crates/snipset-cli/src/db/init.rs cover only some names; everything else falls to `_ => format!("{column} TEXT")` and is emitted as a bare nullable TEXT. That is how twelve columns come out with the wrong declared type, NOT NULL flag, or DEFAULT compared with what the desktop app declares, including research_tag which the app declares INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L28] The constants are only column NAMES and the type comes from column_definition, so adding a name without a matching arm changes the emitted schema with nothing on the name-level check noticing.

nodes.label: Fingerprint name-versus-shape agreement
nodes.summary: Reused id. Same claim. GROUP_COLUMNS and SNIPPET_COLUMNS are the shared input to both snipset init's CREATE TABLE builder and the CLI schema fingerprint, so the two sides agree on column NAMES by construction. Because the fingerprint compares names only, every pre-existing test kept passing while twelve columns carried a different declared shape.

nodes.label: Assert on columns only; the deliberate foreign key and index differences are out of scope
nodes.norm_label: assert on columns only; the deliberate foreign key and index differences are out of scope
nodes.summary: A deliberate scope limit on the parity test: it compares declared type, notnull and dflt_value for every column the app declares, and asserts nothing about table constraints, foreign keys, indexes, triggers or row order. Structural differences found during the work were recorded in the report instead: the CLI's snippets table lacks FOREIGN KEY (group_id) REFERENCES groups(uuid), and it creates none of idx_snippets_keyword, idx_snippets_group_id or idx_snippets_created_at, so the app's uniqueness constraint on keyword does not exist in an init-created database. Column order was checked and matches.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L00051] The CLI's `snippets` table deliberately lacks the app's `FOREIGN KEY (group_id) REFERENCES groups(uuid)` clause; that structural difference is out of scope and asserting on it would create a permanent red test.

nodes.label: A schema parser that yields zero columns must fail the test loudly
nodes.norm_label: a schema parser that yields zero columns must fail the test loudly
nodes.summary: Vacuity guard on the narrow parsers. Both the CREATE TABLE block reader and the migration-array reader assert their anchor occurs exactly once and assert the extracted column list is non-empty, so a parser that silently stops matching (anchor renamed, indentation changed, array restructured) turns the test red instead of green. The task also required a column definition to fail to parse rather than be skipped, in the narrow-parser-fails-loudly style already used in fingerprint_test.rs.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L53] A parser that yields zero columns would make every per-column loop a no-op and the parity test would pass while checking nothing; fingerprint_test.rs has the precedent.

nodes.label: NOT NULL is read from an explicit token pair, never inferred from PRIMARY KEY
nodes.norm_label: not null is read from an explicit token pair, never inferred from primary key
nodes.summary: Judgement call recorded in the final report. The notnull expectation is set only by an adjacent NOT NULL token pair in the app's declaration. It is deliberately not derived from a PRIMARY KEY clause, which is what a reader would otherwise assume.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L09145] SQLite's `pragma_table_info` reports `notnull=0` for a `TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, so inferring would have manufactured false failures on both `uuid` columns.

nodes.label: Default literals compared with one outer quote pair stripped from both sides, none kept distinct from empty
nodes.norm_label: default literals compared with one outer quote pair stripped from both sides, none kept distinct from empty
nodes.summary: Judgement call on dflt_value comparison. The app-side literal is kept verbatim including its quotes because pragma_table_info returns DEFAULT 'Text' as 'Text' with quotes. For the comparison itself one matching outer quote pair is stripped from both sides, so a pure quoting difference cannot fail the test, while the <none> sentinel stays distinct from the empty literal so DEFAULT '' and no default remain different facts. Raw literals are printed in the failure report.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L9144] Stripping one matching outer pair from both sides keeps a quoting difference from failing the test, but collapsing <none> into the empty literal would erase the distinction between DEFAULT '' and no default at all.

nodes.label: schema.rs and the migration arrays currently agree, so the reconciliation disagreement branch never fires
nodes.norm_label: schema.rs and the migration arrays currently agree, so the reconciliation disagreement branch never fires
nodes.summary: The test reconciles two sources into one expectation per column: the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS groups/snippets blocks in schema.rs, which are authoritative for a fresh database, and the group_cols / snippet_cols migration arrays, which cover columns added after the table was created. Where a column appears in both, the two parsed shapes are compared and a disagreement is reported rather than one being silently preferred. Measured result for groups (12 columns) and snippets (26 columns): the two sources agree on every shared column, is_deleted being INTEGER DEFAULT 0 in both and image_data TEXT in both, so the disagreement branch is implemented but currently dead.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L9140] Agreement between the two sources was verified rather than assumed, and the cross-check is kept so a future divergence surfaces instead of being silently resolved in favour of one file.

nodes.label: The requested RED parity test arrived GREEN because the parent session fixed the production code mid-flight
nodes.norm_label: the requested red parity test arrived green because the parent session fixed the production code mid-flight
nodes.summary: The task specified that the test must be RED on delivery, must not be weakened until green, and must not get an allowlist of known-divergent columns. It turned out green anyway: while the subagent was working, the parent session fixed column_definition in crates/snipset-cli/src/db/init.rs (commit 2030dbccc, later rebased as 824a83e7b) and committed the test. Re-simulating the exact parsers against real SQLite gives zero divergences against the fixed code. The deliverable is therefore the GREEN control at this stage, and the twelve-column table in the report is the pre-fix evidence the test caught.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L9133] The expected RED evidence no longer existed to be captured, because the production fix the test was meant to expose landed while the test was being written.

nodes.label: A hand-written simulation of the parser misled the fix: filter instead of take_while produced a false alarm
nodes.norm_label: a hand-written simulation of the parser misled the fix: filter instead of take_while produced a false alarm
nodes.summary: The declared-type parser was briefly changed to also stop at NULL and KEY, with a doc comment claiming this was needed to prevent false failures on TEXT NOT NULL and TEXT PRIMARY KEY. Re-running the simulation with the original keyword-only terminator set gave identical output on every sample, which falsified the premise. take_while stops at NOT and at PRIMARY and never reaches their operands, so the original code was already correct; the Python simulation had used a filter comprehension, which does keep scanning, and that was the actual defect. Both edits were reverted and the inaccurate comment removed.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L9146] A comment asserting a bug the code never had is worse than no comment, so the change was reverted once the simulation rather than the Rust was shown to be wrong.

nodes.label: Zero-subagent compiler policy
nodes.summary: Reused id. Same claim. The first hard constraint of the task, quoted from the repository AGENTS.md: no cargo, rustc, clippy, nextest, mold or bun, locally or over ssh, and no ssh at all. Verification was therefore re-reading plus simulating both parsers and pragma_table_info against real SQLite in Python. Compilation and the actual test run are explicitly reported as unverified.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-10-01 - write-init-type-parity-test [ses_f08bc0fb7ffexOnd7Om7z4BEAk].md:L00023] You cannot verify your own work compiles; that is deliberate, the parent does it.

nodes.label: tinyfish connect wrote the skill to ~/.agents/skills but never to ~/.config/opencode/skills
nodes.norm_label: tinyfish connect wrote the skill to agents skills but never to opencode skills
nodes.summary: `npx -y @tiny-fish/cli@latest connect --all --api-key ... --skip-launch` registered the TinyFish MCP server for Cline and OpenCode and reported the use-tinyfish skill installed for both, but on disk only ~/.agents/skills/use-tinyfish existed. ~/.config/opencode/skills/use-tinyfish had to be created separately, along with the ~/.gemini/config/skills and antigravity builtin copies, which is what install.sh section 6b in the ai-skills repository now does. The same connect run also reported API-key auth covering the whole flow, so no browser sign-in was needed, and it warned that the CLI wants Node >=24 while the machine runs v22.23.3, which was EBADENGINE warning only and did not block the install.

nodes.label: A vendored skill copy carries an upstream / refresh / revert provenance footer
nodes.norm_label: a vendored skill copy carries an upstream / refresh / revert provenance footer
nodes.summary: skills/use-tinyfish/SKILL.md in the ai-skills repository is a copy of the file tinyfish connect wrote to ~/.agents/skills/use-tinyfish, appended with a Provenance section naming the upstream (tinyfish-io/tinyfish-cookbook, skill use-tinyfish), the exact command to re-run and re-copy to refresh it, and the full revert path: rm -rf the skill dir, drop the block from install.sh, re-run install.sh, and optionally remove the deployed copies under ~/.agents/skills, ~/.config/opencode/skills, ~/.gemini/config/skills and ~/.claude/skills. install.sh section 6b deploys it as a single-file skill to every harness target, with the ~/.claude target conditional like the rest of the script.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-30 - tinyfish-setup-and-connection-check [ses_f0db9f30cffeJYpA76JszqgVJy].md:L4800] The revert instructions are written into the SKILL.md footer and the install.sh section 6b comment rather than left in the session, because the next session cannot read this conversation.

nodes.label: The deep-research workflow must name one evidence tool, enforced by a validator check
nodes.norm_label: the deep research workflow must name one evidence tool, enforced by a validator check
nodes.summary: The ai-skills repository was changed from tool-agnostic research to TinyFish-mandated research in three places that must agree: an Evidence Gathering section in templates/deep-research-report-template.md, an Evidence Gathering subsection in the master skill (Super Ultra Code Plan Implementation.md), and a new check 3f in scripts/validate-skill.mjs that fails unless the literal use-tinyfish is present in both files. Every inline citation index must map to a source actually retrieved through that ladder, and a cited-but-unfetched source fails the report exactly like an unread one.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-30 - tinyfish-setup-and-connection-check [ses_f0db9f30cffeJYpA76JszqgVJy].md:L05550] Deep-research evidence contract: the workflow must name its evidence tool.\n// Without a named tool each agent improvises its own browsing and citations stop\n// being reproducible.

nodes.label: Lightest-tool ladder: search, then fetch, then agent only for pages that need interaction
nodes.norm_label: lightest tool ladder search fetch agent
nodes.summary: The prescribed escalation order inside the Evidence Gathering section: search to discover sources, fetch the best results for full content, and escalate to agent only for pages that need interaction such as forms, login or dynamic extraction. The rule is stated as never starting with the heaviest tool.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-30 - tinyfish-setup-and-connection-check [ses_f0db9f30cffeJYpA76JszqgVJy].md:L5488] Search and fetch are the cheap retrieval tools and agent is the paid browser automation path, so the order is fixed so the expensive one is never the entry point.

nodes.label: Deep-research rule changes went in the template, not in the snippets, to avoid Snipset database drift
nodes.norm_label: deep research rule changes went in the template, not in the snippets, to avoid snipset database drift
nodes.summary: The two snippet files under snippets/ were deliberately left untouched even though they invoke the deep-research phase. Editing the shared template instead makes both of them carry the new TinyFish evidence rule for free, and keeps `bun run snippets:check` reporting the trigger prompts as matching the Snipset database rather than as drift.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-30 - tinyfish-setup-and-connection-check [ses_f0db9f30cffeJYpA76JszqgVJy].md:L5618] Both snippets call the deep-research phase via the template, so the rule travels without editing the files that are synced against the Snipset database and triggering drift.
